source.title: Concept-Guided Interpretability via Neural Chunking
source.authors: Shu-Chen Wu; S. Alaniz; Shyamgopal Karthik; Peter Dayan; Eric Schulz; Zeynep Akata

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses prior claims of representational convergence as motivation, but its own experiments study whether activity chunks reflect input structure. It does not measure whether representations of different models become more similar, or whether that similarity rises with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The paper cites convergence findings and proposes that data regularities explain them, but its experiments do not compare model-to-model distances or similarity. Its cross-model RNN result reports similar chunk counts and alignment of chunks to input patterns, not convergence of representations between models. Other reported chunk decoding, grafting, and freezing results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites convergence findings (incl. the Platonic Representation Hypothesis) as motivation and proposes that data regularities explain them (the Reflection Hypothesis). Its experiments test whether each model's activity contains chunks mirroring input patterns. They never compare representations between models with a similarity, mapping or stitching measure, nor vary scale against alignment. The cross-RNN result (SI D.1, D.5) compares chunk counts across RNNs of 12/24/48 hidden units, not pairwise representational alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors propose the Reflection Hypothesis: neural population activity mirrors regularities in training data. They offer it as an explanation of reported representational convergence, then use chunking (DSC, PA, UCD) to extract interpretable, causally effective concept units in RNNs and LLMs. They do not directly test cross-model convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The paper’s chunk extraction methods are not a reproduction or measurement of the original representation-similarity methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Simple RNNs with 12, 24 and 48 hidden units trained on the same sequences yield a similar number of extracted chunks. Their activity reflects the same input regularities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks of different widths trained on the same data each contain activity chunks mirroring the data's recurring patterns. This is a within-model reflection of data structure, not cross-model alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Population-averaging chunks predicting the top-100 English words are extracted in LLaMA-3-8B, T5-small, RWKV-169m and Mamba-130m, each decoded within its own model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-encoding population chunks are found across diverse LM architectures, with no cross-model correspondence tested.

record.problems: The cross-architecture RNN result is qualitative in the text and does not report a pairwise representation-similarity measure or scale/performance comparison. The text does not specify the individual architectures in that comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Chunk decoding, concept grafting/freezing, and narrative-schema results were left out because they do not measure cross-model representational convergence or another version of the claim.

untested.parts: All: no cross-model representational similarity measured, and none tracked against scale or capability.
All: no vision-language or paired-data alignment.
All: no comparison of features or subspaces across seeds of the same architecture.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests between models.
All: concept chunks are extracted separately in LLaMA-3, T5, RWKV and Mamba, but the chunks are not compared across models.
All: no comparison of similarity metrics or input distributions.
All: the data-regularity explanation of convergence is proposed but not tested against cross-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The PRH (arXiv:2405.07987) is cited only as motivation. The multi-LLM decoding results (Fig. 5, SI E.5) could be mistaken for V5 evidence, but no cross-model feature matching is performed.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models become more aligned as size or capability rises; pairwise representation similarity across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation alignment test, and no scale or performance sweep.
No test of shared features or subspaces across initialization seeds of the same architecture.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability between models.
No cross-model recurrence test of interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
No comparison of representation-convergence metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No test of the completeness, plateau, or causes of cross-model representational alignment.

rows.subject: RNNs with different architectures (aggregate; individual architectures not stated)
rows.stage_stated: trained on synthetic sequences; training details for this cross-architecture comparison not stated
rows.operation_detail: Applied unsupervised chunk discovery to RNNs and assessed structural regularities in the extracted chunks.

conditions.value: simple sequence containing repeated ABCD; further cross-architecture details not stated

rows.measure: Qualitative cross-model consistency of chunk structure, including chunk counts and alignment to input patterns.
rows.value: The text reports consistent structural regularities across models, with similar chunk counts and alignment to input patterns.
rows.note: This is a result about each model’s chunks reflecting input structure, not a measurement of pairwise similarity between the models’ representations or convergence with scale.
rows.check: Subject is mis-stated. SI D.5 and Figs 10–11 show the 'different architectures' are simple RNNs differing only in hidden size (12, 24, 48 units), not distinct architecture types. The measure is the number of DSC-extracted chunks and a qualitative view of activity, not representational similarity between models. Locator should include SI D.5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
